# Orca plugin manifest reference

<!-- Generated by `pnpm generate:plugin-schemas` from src/shared/plugins. Do not edit. -->

The orca-plugin.json file at the root of an Orca plugin (manifest format 2).

Add `"$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stablyai/orca/main/docs/schemas/plugins/orca-plugin.v2.schema.json"` to `orca-plugin.json` for completion and inline errors in your editor.
`Since` is the first Orca release that reads the field; raise `engines.orca` when you use a newer one.

## Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$schema` | string | no | 1.4.245 | JSON Schema URL for editor completion. Ignored by Orca. |
| `manifestVersion` | `2` | yes | 1.4.245 | Manifest format. Use 2 for new plugins. |
| `execution` | `"data"` \| `"declarative"` \| `"sandboxed-ui"` \| `"trusted-worker"` | yes | 1.4.245 | Most authority the plugin needs, least first: `data` (themes, syntaxes, translations), `declarative` (commands, shortcuts, recipes), `sandboxed-ui` (panels), `trusted-worker` (`main` and events). Contributions beyond it fail validation. Example: `"data"` |
| `id` | string | yes | 1.4.160 | Plugin id, kebab-case. The install identity is `<publisher>.<id>`. The reserved names `constructor` and `prototype` are refused. Example: `"gleam-syntax"` |
| `publisher` | string | yes | 1.4.160 | Publisher slug, kebab-case. Must be the GitHub or GitLab user or organization that owns the repository (`acme` for `github.com/acme/gleam-syntax`), or the official and community catalogs reject the listing. The reserved names `constructor` and `prototype` are refused. The publishers `stablyai`, `official`, `anthropic`, `openai`, `github` and any starting `orca` (any case), and ids starting `orca-`, install only from Orca's official catalog. Example: `"acme"` |

## PanelContribution

A sidebar panel. Requires the `sandboxed-ui` execution profile or higher.

| Field | Type | Required | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | 1.4.160 | Panel id, unique among this plugin's panels. The reserved names `constructor` and `prototype` are refused. Example: `"dashboard"` |
| `title` | string | yes | 1.4.160 | Title shown on the panel tab and its tooltip. Example: `"Dashboard"` |
| `icon` | `"activity"` \| `"bar-chart-3"` \| `"bell"` \| `"blocks"` \| `"book"` \| `"bot"` \| `"bug"` \| `"calendar"` \| `"cloud"` \| `"code"` \| `"database"` \| `"file-text"` \| `"flag"` \| `"folder"` \| `"gauge"` \| `"globe"` \| `"hammer"` \| `"layers"` \| `"lightbulb"` \| `"package"` \| `"plug"` \| `"puzzle"` \| `"rocket"` \| `"star"` \| `"terminal"` \| `"wrench"` \| `"zap"` | no | 1.4.160 | Icon shown in the right-sidebar activity bar. Defaults to `plug`. Example: `"database"` |
| `entry` | string | yes | 1.4.160 | HTML file, relative to the plugin root, rendered inside a sandboxed panel frame. Relative to the plugin root; `..` segments and Windows device names such as `CON` are refused. Example: `"dist/panel.html"` |

## CommandContribution

A command palette entry. Requires the `declarative` execution profile or higher.

| Field | Type | Required | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | 1.4.160 | Command id, unique among this plugin's commands. Dotted namespaces are allowed. Example: `"jupyter.restartKernel"` |
| `title` | string | yes | 1.4.160 | Title shown in the command palette. Example: `"Restart kernel"` |
| `when` | `"global"` \| `"workspace"` | no | 1.4.160 | Where the command is available. `workspace` hides it when no workspace is active. Defaults to `global`. |
| `action` | `"worktree.history.back"` \| `"worktree.history.forward"` \| `"sidebar.left.toggle"` \| `"sidebar.sleepingWorkspaces.toggle"` \| `"floatingWorkspace.maximize"` \| `"tab.rename"` \| `"workspace.rename"` \| `"workspace.openBoard"` \| `"view.tasks"` \| `"sidebar.right.toggle"` \| `"sidebar.explorer.toggle"` \| `"sidebar.search.toggle"` \| `"sidebar.sourceControl.toggle"` \| `"sidebar.checks.toggle"` \| `"sidebar.ports.toggle"` | no | 1.4.160 | Built-in Orca action this command runs. A command with an action is declarative and never starts the plugin worker; one without needs `main`. Example: `"view.tasks"` |

## EventContribution

An event subscription. Requires `main`, the `trusted-worker` execution profile and the capability of the event's domain: `workspace:read` for workspace events, `agent:read` for agent events.

| Field | Type | Required | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `on` | `"workspace.created"` \| `"workspace.removed"` \| `"agent.status.changed"` | yes | 1.4.160 | Event delivered to the plugin worker. |

## LanguagePackContribution

An interface translation.

| Field | Type | Required | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `locale` | string | yes | 1.4.160 | BCP 47 locale the pack translates Orca into. Each locale appears once, ignoring case. Example: `"pt-BR"` |
| `path` | string | yes | 1.4.160 | JSON file of translated interface strings. Relative to the plugin root; `..` segments and Windows device names such as `CON` are refused. Example: `"locales/pt-BR.json"` |
| `displayName` | string | no | 1.4.245 | Native-language name for the Settings picker. Omitted packs show `{locale} — {pluginKey}`. Example: `"Português (Brasil)"` |

## KeybindingContribution

A keyboard shortcut for a command.

| Field | Type | Required | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `command` | string | yes | 1.4.160 | Id of a command this plugin contributes in `contributes.commands`. Example: `"jupyter.restartKernel"` |
| `key` | string | yes | 1.4.160 | Key chord Orca recognizes, such as `Mod+Shift+K`. `Mod` is Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. Each chord may be bound once on every platform. Example: `"Mod+Shift+K"` |
| `when` | `"global"` \| `"workspace"` | no | 1.4.160 | Where the shortcut is active; must match its command's `when`. |

## SyntaxContribution

Syntax highlighting for one language.

| Field | Type | Required | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | Language id, unique among this plugin's syntaxes. The reserved names `constructor` and `prototype` are refused. Example: `"gleam"` |
| `title` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | Language name shown in the editor. Example: `"Gleam"` |
| `scopeName` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | The grammar's root TextMate scope, unique among this plugin's syntaxes. Example: `"source.gleam"` |
| `path` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | TextMate grammar JSON file. Relative to the plugin root; `..` segments and Windows device names such as `CON` are refused. Example: `"syntaxes/gleam.tmLanguage.json"` |
| `configuration` | string | no | 1.4.245 | Language configuration JSON file: comments, brackets and auto-closing pairs. Relative to the plugin root; `..` segments and Windows device names such as `CON` are refused. Example: `"syntaxes/language-configuration.json"` |
| `extensions` | string[] | no | 1.4.245 | File-name suffixes, with the dot, this language opens, ignoring case. A longer suffix such as `.excalidraw.json` wins over a shorter one, and a file named only the suffix never matches. At most 32. Example: `[".gleam"]` |
| `filenames` | string[] | no | 1.4.245 | Exact file names this language opens, ignoring case; a name beats any extension. Names must be portable: no path separators, `.`, `..` or characters Windows forbids. At most 32. Example: `["gleam.toml"]` |

## CustomEditorContribution

An editor for the listed files, shown in the editor tab beside Source. It must list at least one extension or file name. Requires the `sandboxed-ui` execution profile or higher.

| Field | Type | Required | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | Editor id, unique among this plugin's custom editors. The reserved names `constructor` and `prototype` are refused. Example: `"excalidraw"` |
| `title` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | Name shown in the editor's view toggle beside Source, and on the tab of a file it opens. Example: `"Excalidraw"` |
| `icon` | string | no | 1.4.245 | Square image shown on the tab of a file this editor opens. Defaults to the plugin icon. PNG, WEBP, static, at least 128×128, square, at most 256 KB. Relative to the plugin root; `..` segments and Windows device names such as `CON` are refused. Example: `"images/editor-icon.png"` |
| `extensions` | string[] | no | 1.4.245 | File-name suffixes, with the dot, this editor opens, ignoring case. A longer suffix such as `.excalidraw.json` wins over a shorter one, and a file named only the suffix never matches. At most 32. Example: `[".excalidraw",".excalidraw.json"]` |
| `filenames` | string[] | no | 1.4.245 | Exact file names this editor opens, ignoring case; a name beats any extension. Names must be portable: no path separators, `.`, `..` or characters Windows forbids. At most 32. Example: `[]` |
| `entry` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | HTML file rendered inside a sandboxed editor frame, like a panel. It receives the open document and posts edits back; it never gets a file path or file system. It is trusted code: install editors you trust. Relative to the plugin root; `..` segments and Windows device names such as `CON` are refused. Example: `"editor/index.html"` |
| `priority` | `"default"` \| `"option"` | no | 1.4.245 | `default` (the default) opens matching files in this editor; `option` only offers it in the view toggle, so files open in Source. Files Orca opens itself (such as `.json`, `.ts`, `.md`, `.csv`, `.yaml`, lockfiles and `.env` files) always behave as `option`. Example: `"default"` |
| `contentKind` | `"text"` \| `"bytes"` | no | 1.4.245 | `text` (the default) sends the file as text and accepts full-text edits. `bytes` sends the file's raw bytes, for binary formats such as spreadsheets, and accepts full-byte edits. Example: `"bytes"` |

## NewFileContribution

A kind of untitled file the user can create from the tab bar + menu or the command palette, in the active workspace.

| Field | Type | Required | Since | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | New-file id, unique among this plugin's new files. The reserved names `constructor` and `prototype` are refused. Example: `"drawing"` |
| `title` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | Menu item shown in the tab bar + menu and the command palette. Example: `"New Excalidraw drawing"` |
| `extension` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | Suffix, with the dot, of the untitled file it creates. The file opens in whatever editor takes that suffix, such as a custom editor from this plugin. Example: `".excalidraw"` |
| `template` | string | no | 1.4.245 | UTF-8 file copied into the new file, at most 256 KB. Without one the file starts empty. Relative to the plugin root; `..` segments and Windows device names such as `CON` are refused. Example: `"templates/empty.excalidraw"` |
| `icon` | string | no | 1.4.245 | Square image shown beside the menu item. Defaults to the plugin icon. PNG, WEBP, static, at least 128×128, square, at most 256 KB. Relative to the plugin root; `..` segments and Windows device names such as `CON` are refused. Example: `"images/editor-icon.png"` |

| `alt` | string | yes | 1.4.245 | What the image shows, for screen readers. Required. Example: `"The Dusk theme on a terminal"` |

## Versions and compatibility

- **What runs is strict.** Orca refuses a manifest with any key it does not know, at every level, so an older Orca never silently ignores something a plugin relies on.
- **`engines.orca` is the only version gate.** It must be at least the newest `Since` of every field and every value (capability, event, built-in action) the manifest uses. `pnpm validate:plugin` and catalog CI enforce it, so an older Orca can always say "requires Orca >=X (this is Y)" instead of listing unknown fields.
- **`pluginApi` is optional.** It names the major version of the host API ([reference](plugin-host-api.md)), which only grows within major 1; Orca refuses a major it does not implement. Only `sandboxed-ui` and `trusted-worker` plugins call that API, so `data` and `declarative` plugins must leave it out.
- **`terminal:send` needs `trusted-worker`.** Panels get no host method that types into a terminal, so Orca refuses the capability on any other profile instead of asking the user to grant something the plugin can never use.
- **New fields, contribution points and values are additive.** They arrive with a `Since` version; nothing else changes. `manifestVersion` rises only if an existing field changes meaning.
- **Deprecation.** A field to be removed is marked deprecated here and keeps working for at least one release; it is removed only together with a higher `engines.orca` requirement, and its name is never reused.
- **Reserved contribution points.** `contributes.agentHarnesses`, `skills`, `mcpServers`, `hooks`, `taskSources`, `connections`, `settings`, `statusBarItems` and `sidebarCards` are held for planned features and must stay empty until their format is defined. Each will arrive as an additive point with its own `Since`, without a new manifest format. `skills`, `mcpServers` and `hooks` keep the meaning agent-plugin formats such as Claude Code's give them; `agents` stays unclaimed because those formats use it for subagent files.

## Planned contribution points

Each reserved point is planned as declared data that Orca renders and enforces, never arbitrary plugin UI. The intended shapes, which may still change:

- `taskSources`: Issue and task providers such as Asana, Linear or Jira, declared as data that a worker fills with tasks.
- `connections`: Account providers with a host-run sign-in, so a plugin never handles credentials itself.
- `agentHarnesses`: New coding-agent harnesses described as data: how to launch them and read their status.
- `statusBarItems`: Declarative status bar widgets (label, icon, tooltip) whose values a worker updates.
- `sidebarCards`: Declarative left-sidebar cards with fixed layouts whose values a worker updates.
- `mcpServers`: MCP server definitions that Orca offers to the agents it launches.
- `skills`: Agent skills shipped as files that Orca installs for the agents it launches.
- `hooks`: Agent lifecycle hooks, such as before and after a tool call, for the agents Orca launches.
- `settings`: Typed plugin settings that Orca renders in its own settings UI.

## Legacy format 1

Orca still loads `"manifestVersion": 1` manifests (read since 1.4.160), but new plugins should use format 2. Format 1 differs in three ways:

- It has no `execution` field. Orca derives the least profile that can run what the manifest declares.
- Unknown top-level keys are ignored instead of rejected.
- The published JSON Schema does not describe it, so editors offer no completion for it.
